title: ScoreResponse
description: Answer of the speech service's POST /v1/score: one verdict per expected phoneme, grouped by the words of the reference text. Carries no learner-facing prose.

thresholdsVersion.description: Version of the GOP thresholds that produced the verdicts; a verdict is only comparable with another of the same version.

verdict.description: From the GOP and the thresholds named by thresholdsVersion: correct above the upper threshold, wrong below the lower one, unclear between. Only wrong is reported to the learner as an error.

text.description: The word as written in referenceText.

start.description: Character offset of the word in referenceText.

end.description: Character offset just past the word.

verdict.description: The worst verdict among the word's phonemes: wrong if any is wrong, else unclear if any is unclear, else correct. Unclear when the word has no phonemes.

reference.description: Which reference accent the word was scored against: each word is scored against both and keeps the one with fewer wrong, then fewer unclear, then the higher mean GOP; a tie keeps en-us.

expected.description: espeak IPA token the reference calls for.

heard.description: When unclear or wrong: the phoneme the model found most likely in the expected phoneme's frames. Null when correct.

gop.description: Goodness of pronunciation in nats; higher is better.

startMs.description: Start of the aligned frames, from the start of the recording.

feedback.description: Present exactly when the verdict is wrong; null when correct or unclear. Which fixed explanation to show, never the text itself.

The client renders messageKey + '.why' (what went wrong) and messageKey + '.how' (what to do with the mouth) from its message catalogue, filling the {name} placeholders from params. The service sends no prose.

expected.description: espeak IPA token the reference calls for.

heard.description: The phoneme's own heard value, raw (a variant such as tʰ is not folded).

word.description: The reference word that holds the phoneme, as written.
